[P0] Live-key guard inside getStripe, one client factory, and a rail that needs the key AND a webhook secret (ST-0; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.1 "Safety first", M-25, C2, C6). DO THIS ITEM FIRST: the clone .env holds a live Stripe key.
CHANGE: (1) New server/src/platform/billing/stripeEnv.ts, pure (no Stripe SDK import, no logger, no import of flags.ts): stripeSecretKey(env) = trimmed STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or null; stripeKeyMode(env) = 'none' | 'test' | 'live' (live when the key starts with sk_live_ or rk_live_); liveKeyAllowed(env) = env.VERCEL_ENV === 'production' || parseBoolEnv(env.STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE_KEY_OUTSIDE_PRODUCTION); stripeKeyUsable(env) = { usable, reason: 'missing' | 'live_key_outside_production' | null }; stripeWebhookSecrets(env) = the values of ROBOAPPLY_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET then STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, each split on commas, trimmed, empties and duplicates dropped; stripeRailReady(env) = stripeKeyUsable(env).usable && stripeWebhookSecrets(env).length > 0. (2) server/src/platform/billing/stripeClient.ts getStripe (today lines 16-24): keep the test seam first (line 17); then return null when stripeKeyUsable is false, logging ONCE per process at error level for live_key_outside_production (say which variable allows it; never print the key or any part of it beyond the word live); build the client with new Stripe(key, { maxNetworkRetries: 2, appInfo: { name: 'RoboApply', url: 'https://www.roboapply.io' } }) (line 21). Because every caller goes through this factory (rails/stripe.ts:76, subscriptions.ts:238/316/376, features/credits/service.ts:238, RoboApplyBillingService.ts:131, routes/stripeWebhook.ts:33), checkout, catalog sync, cancel, switch, portal, refund and webhook are all refused with a live key outside production. (3) The second construction site: server/src/roboapply/v2/services/RAAdminOperationsService.ts lines 89-90 calls new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, { timeout: 6000, maxNetworkRetries: 0 }) and would read invoices with the live key from a dev machine. Replace it with getStripe() from platform/billing/stripeClient.js, pass { timeout: 6000, maxNetworkRetries: 0 } as the per-request options of its invoices.list calls so the 20 s scan budget holds, and keep coverage 'not_configured' when getStripe() is null. (4) server/src/platform/billing/rails/stripe.ts isConfigured (line 73) returns stripeRailReady(env). (5) server/src/platform/flags.ts case 'pay.stripe' (line 329) becomes brand.paymentRails.includes('stripe') && stripeRailReady(env): one import and one line, nothing else in that file. (6) Env fixtures of existing tests that name STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and expect the rail or the flag to be on get STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: 'whsec_test' added (rails/registry.test.ts ENV line 14, rails/rails.test.ts ENV line 15, integration/RoboApplyBillingService.stripe.test.ts PRICES line 39, flags.test.ts:140, features/brand/routes.test.ts:10 and :43, features/features.test.ts:263, features/credits/credits.test.ts, accountV2.test.ts, money.test.ts). Adding a variable to a shared env fixture is allowed; the body of a test named for an Alipay rule A1-A12 (written by the parity wave) is never edited.
ACCEPT: (section 9) A live key with VERCEL_ENV != production makes getStripe return null: the rail is unavailable and no Stripe call of any kind is attempted; STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE_KEY_OUTSIDE_PRODUCTION=true restores it; a key without a webhook secret lists plans with amounts and payments_disabled. Added: an sk_test_ key works in any runtime; with VERCEL_ENV=production a live key works; the refusal is logged once and the log line contains no key material; GET /api/v1/public/brand reports pay.stripe false until both the key and a webhook secret are set; no file under server/src, api/ or scripts/ other than stripeClient.ts contains "new Stripe(".
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/stripeEnv.test.ts (new: key modes, the override, comma-separated and duplicated webhook secrets, readiness matrix); server/src/platform/billing/stripeClient.test.ts (new: with vi.mock('stripe') a live key outside production constructs nothing and returns null; a test key constructs once with maxNetworkRetries 2 and appInfo; setStripeClientForTests still wins); server/src/platform/billing/stripeSingleClient.test.ts (new: reads the source tree and fails if "new Stripe(" appears outside stripeClient.ts); rails/registry.test.ts and flags.test.ts (key without webhook secret: rail and flag off); RAAdminOperationsService.test.ts (payments report uses the shared factory; no client is built for a refused key). Every test uses setStripeClientForTests or a mocked SDK; none reaches Stripe.

[P0] Stripe Products and Prices synced from the catalog by lookup key, created on first use (ST-1; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.1 "Catalog sync", M-15)
CHANGE: New server/src/platform/billing/stripeCatalog.ts. Products with fixed ids: ra_pro (pro_weekly, pro_monthly, pro_quarterly), ra_pro_student (student_monthly, student_quarterly), ra_pro_week_pass (pro_week_pass), ra_practice_pack (practice_pack_5, practice_pack_15); products.create({ id, name, metadata: { product: 'roboapply' } }, { idempotencyKey: 'catalog:product:<id>' }) and the Stripe error code resource_already_exists counts as success. stripeLookupKey(planKey, currency, amountMinor) = 'ra_<planKey>_<currency lower case>_<amountMinor>_incl' (example ra_pro_monthly_usd_2499_incl); parseStripeLookupKey is its inverse. resolveStripePriceId(stripe, plan, currency: 'USD' | 'TWD'): (a) a pin (plan.stripePriceId for USD, plan.twdPrice.stripePriceId for TWD) is returned as is, with no Stripe call; (b) a memory cache per Stripe client holding one in-flight promise per lookup key (a rejected promise is removed); (c) prices.list({ lookup_keys: [key], active: true, limit: 1 }) (at most 10 keys per call); a found price must match unit_amount, currency and recurring, otherwise throw payment_provider_error and log (never transfer a lookup key); (d) prices.create({ product, currency, unit_amount, lookup_key, tax_behavior: 'inclusive', recurring: week -> { interval: 'week', interval_count: 1 }, month -> { interval: 'month', interval_count: 1 }, quarter -> { interval: 'month', interval_count: 3 }, none for the pass and packs, metadata: { product: 'roboapply', planKey } }, { idempotencyKey: 'catalog:<lookup_key>' }); if create fails because the key is already taken (another instance won the race), list once more. planKeyForPrice(price | priceId, env): price.metadata.planKey -> parse price.lookup_key -> env pins (planKeyForStripePrice) -> null (the legacy map priceIdToMockPlanKey stays in the service). syncStripeCatalog(stripe, env) resolves every MVP plan once (optional warm-up; never required). Every Stripe failure becomes BillingError('payment_provider_error') (HTTP 502). getPlanCatalog stays synchronous and never calls Stripe. Export the module from server/src/platform/billing/index.ts.
ACCEPT: (section 9) Empty env + key: every MVP plan resolves a price at the default amount; a second resolve makes no call; two concurrent resolves create one price; a pin skips the sync. Added: quarterly is created with interval month and interval_count 3; the pass and packs have no recurring; every created price carries tax_behavior inclusive, the lookup key and metadata.planKey; a changed amount gives a new lookup key and leaves the old price untouched; a Stripe failure makes checkout answer 502 while GET /billing/plans still answers; planKeyForPrice resolves a synced price from metadata, from the lookup key alone, and a pinned id from env.

env: STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE_KEY_OUTSIDE_PRODUCTION: true lets a live Stripe key work when VERCEL_ENV is not production (default unset = refused)
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET / ROBOAPPLY_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: now REQUIRED for the Stripe rail to be available; a comma-separated list is accepted (default unset = plans listed, payments_disabled)
PRICE_<PLANKEY>_USD_CENTS: overrides a RoboApply catalog amount, positive integer cents (default: catalog 999 / 2499 / 5499 / 999 / 999 / 2499 / 1749 / 3799)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_CENTS: read as an alias of PRICE_<PLANKEY>_USD_CENTS (default unset)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>: optional pin of a Stripe price id, honoured only together with an amount variable (default unset = price resolved by the catalog sync)
PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS: Taiwan price in TWD minor units, multiple of 100 (default unset = Taiwan pays USD with the reference line)
STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS: alias of PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD_CENTS; STRIPE_PRICE_<PLANKEY>_TWD: optional pin (default unset)

CHANGE: server/src/roboapply/routes/billing.ts: new POST /checkout/reconcile (requireAuth), body { sessionId: string matching /^cs_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,200}$/ } (zod, strict; 422 invalid_request otherwise). server/src/roboapply/services/RoboApplyBillingService.ts: reconcileCheckoutSession(userId, brand, sessionId): no Stripe client -> 503 stripe_not_configured; stripe.checkout.sessions.retrieve(sessionId); Stripe resource_missing -> 404 not_found; ownership: session.metadata.product === 'roboapply', session.metadata.brand is roboapply or absent, session.metadata.userId === userId, and, when the account already has a Stripe customer, session.customer equals it; any failure -> 403 forbidden with no detail; payment_status not 'paid' (and not 'no_payment_required') -> { status: 'pending' } without side effects; otherwise run applyCheckoutSession(session, stripe) from item 2, the same claimed fulfilment as the webhook (claim billing:checkout:<session>), so a later webhook is a duplicate and a repeated reconcile is a no-op. bundles.title: Refund engine: issueRefund, charge.refunded, disputes, pro-rata withdrawal rule, withdrawPurchase, refund mails (server)
items:
[P0] issueRefund: ownership, payment intent lookup, Stripe idempotency key, one readable record (ST-4 part 1; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.1 "Refunds and disputes", 4.4 "How a refund is executed")
CHANGE: New server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts. issueRefund({ userId, target: { invoiceId } | { checkoutSessionId }, amountMinor?, reason, actor, kind?: 'refund' | 'withdrawal' }, deps): load the billing account; no Stripe client -> rail_not_configured; retrieve the invoice or session and require its customer to equal the account's stripeCustomerId, else BillingError('refund_not_available'); payment intent: for a Checkout Session session.payment_intent; for an invoice stripe.invoicePayments.list({ invoice, limit: 10 }) and the paid payment's payment_intent (current invoices carry payments separately; fall back to a top-level payment_intent when the object has one); none -> refund_not_available; amountMinor, when given, must be a positive integer not above what is still refundable; stripe.refunds.create({ payment_intent, amount when partial, reason: 'requested_by_customer', metadata: { product: 'roboapply', userId, actor, kind, planKey } }, { idempotencyKey: 'refund:<pi>:<amount or full>' }); return { refundId, paymentIntentId, chargeId, amountMinor, currency, full }. issueRefund changes NO entitlement: access changes only in the charge.refunded webhook (item 2), so a refund made in the Stripe Dashboard behaves the same. Deps (db, getStripe, now, sendEmail, invalidate, adjustCredits, grantForPlan) are injectable; defaults import the real ones lazily. Import the module once from server/src/platform/billing/index.ts (this bundle owns index.ts in M2) so its event handlers register at boot; export issueRefund, withdrawPurchase and the types.
ACCEPT: A full refund of an invoice and of a one-time session each call refunds.create once with the right payment intent and idempotency key; a second identical call sends the same key; an invoice of another customer is refused with refund_not_available and no Stripe write; a partial amount is passed through; nothing in the database changes except what item 2 does on the webhook.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.test.ts (new; createFakePrisma + fake Stripe with invoices.retrieve, invoicePayments.list, checkout.sessions.retrieve, refunds.create; installed with setStripeClientForTests): the cases above. No test calls Stripe.
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts, stripeRefunds.test.ts, index.ts

[P0] charge.refunded: a full refund reverses the right entitlement once; a partial refund is recorded and changes no access (ST-4 part 2; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.1 "Refunds and disputes", event table)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts registers a handler for charge.refunded through registerStripeEventHandler (MKT-B1 seam). Steps: (1) owner = findBillingOwnerByCustomer(db, charge.customer); none -> { handled: false } (HTTP 200: the account may be shared with other products). (2) claimBillingEvent(db, userId, 'refund:<charge.id>:<charge.amount_refunded>', 'stripe_refund'); not fresh -> { handled: true, duplicate: true }. (3) Find what was bought from charge.payment_intent: the payment intent's metadata (planKey, set at checkout for the pass and packs) and stripe.checkout.sessions.list({ payment_intent, limit: 1 }) for the session id; for a subscription charge stripe.invoicePayments.list filtered by the payment intent -> the invoice -> invoiceSubscriptionId -> the row. (4) Write one RABillingRefund row (schema below; unique on rail + externalRef '<charge.id>:<amount_refunded>'; kind 'refund', or 'withdrawal' when the refund's metadata.kind says so; full = charge.amount_refunded === charge.amount). (5) Only when full: a practice pack -> the RACreditGrant row packGrantId(userId, 'stripe:<sessionId>') (packs.ts): compute what is left of that pack with allocatePackRemaining, lower the practice balance by that amount through adjustCredits (lib/mockCreditService.ts:691) and set the grant's remaining to 0; the running pass -> subtract the pass length from currentPeriodEnd; if that is not after now, the row becomes tier free, planKey free, status canceled, currentPeriodEnd now, and the practice balance is re-granted at the Free allotment; a subscription invoice -> stripe.subscriptions.cancel(subId, {}, { idempotencyKey: 'refundcancel:<subId>:<charge.id>' }) (access then ends through customer.subscription.deleted) and the period's practice credits are reset to the Free allotment. (6) invalidate entitlements; send billing.refund_issued once (item 5). A partial refund does steps 1-4 and 6 without step 5. Every step is replay-safe; a failure answers 500 so Stripe retries.
ACCEPT: (section 9) Full refund of a pack / pass / subscription reverses the right thing once; replay is a no-op; a partial refund changes no access; a charge of a customer we do not know is ignored with HTTP 200. Added: a pack with 2 of 5 interviews used loses the remaining 3 and keeps nothing negative; a refunded pass stacked on another pass shortens access by one pass length instead of ending it; a refunded subscription invoice cancels the subscription now with the idempotency key; a second partial refund of the same charge (a new amount_refunded) is recorded as a new row; a refund made in the Dashboard (no metadata) is handled the same.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/integration/stripeRefunds.webhook.test.ts (new; events are passed to handleRoboApplyStripeEvent with the fake Prisma and a fake Stripe): one test per acceptance line, each replayed once.
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts, integration/stripeRefunds.webhook.test.ts

[P0] charge.dispute.created: reverse as a full refund and flag the account (ST-4 part 3; MARKET_STRATEGY 5.1 event table)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts registers a handler for charge.dispute.created: retrieve the disputed charge (dispute.charge); owner by the charge's customer, none -> { handled: false }; claim 'dispute:<dispute.id>'; run the full-refund reversal of item 2 step 5 for what the charge bought; write an RABillingRefund row with kind 'dispute', externalRef 'dispute:<dispute.id>', amount and currency of the dispute, actor 'stripe', reason = dispute.reason; log one error-level line for staff (user id, dispute id, amount; no card data). The row is the flag: MKT-B9 lists disputes in the admin console. No mail to the user.
ACCEPT: A dispute on a pass, a pack or a subscription charge reverses the entitlement once and writes one dispute row; a replay changes nothing; a dispute on a charge of an unknown customer answers HTTP 200 handled false.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/integration/stripeRefunds.webhook.test.ts (three kinds + replay + foreign).
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts, integration/stripeRefunds.webhook.test.ts

[P0] Withdrawal rule: full without the waiver, pro-rata for unused days with it, for subscriptions (ST-9 calculator; MARKET_STRATEGY M-21, 4.4 "Statutory withdrawal", C4)
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/refunds.ts computeRefund (today lines 100-153). RefundInput gains periodStart?: Date | null and periodEnd?: Date | null; RefundRule gains 'withdrawal_14d_prorata'; RefundDecision gains prorata: { usedDays: number; periodDays: number } | null and endsAccess: boolean. Rule 1 (lines 125-129) keeps the full refund within 14 days when the waiver was not ticked (first purchases and packs, never renewals). New rule 1b: region is set, the waiver WAS ticked, chargeKind is first_purchase, the plan is an auto-renewing subscription (pro_weekly, pro_monthly, pro_quarterly, student_monthly, student_quarterly) and now is within 14 days of the charge and before periodEnd: eligible with rule withdrawal_14d_prorata, periodDays = round((periodEnd - periodStart) / 1 day), usedDays = min(periodDays, ceil((now - periodStart) / 1 day)), amountMinor = floor(amount * (periodDays - usedDays) / periodDays). Without period bounds rule 1b does not apply (the old rules decide). A used pass and used practice credits keep today's rules (2-4). endsAccess is true for both withdrawal rules. Bump REFUND_POLICY_VERSION.roboapply to 'refund-v2-2026-10' (GoApply's version string is unchanged: its passes are outside this rule). server/src/platform/billing/acknowledgements.ts: export WITHDRAWAL_COUNTRIES (the EU 27 of lines 26-29 + IS, LI, NO of line 31 + GB + TW) as the one list the web mirrors (MKT-B10 adds a test that keeps lib/pricing.ts equal to it); withdrawalRegion (36-43) is unchanged. The waiver sentence (line 71) and its prose version are unchanged until counsel rules (owner list item 13).
ACCEPT: (section 9) A German subscriber who ticked the waiver and withdraws on day 5 of 30 is quoted 25/30 of the price. Added: 2499 cents -> 2082; the same buyer without the waiver is quoted 2499; day 15 -> not eligible under the withdrawal rules; a Norwegian and a Taiwanese buyer get the same rule; a US buyer gets none; a renewal never qualifies; a pass with the waiver falls to the 48-hour rule; the decision carries endsAccess true and the prorata numbers.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/refunds.test.ts (the table above, boundaries at the purchase instant, day 14 and period end); server/src/platform/billing/acknowledgements.test.ts (new: WITHDRAWAL_COUNTRIES has 32 entries and every one maps to a region).
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/refunds.ts, refunds.test.ts, acknowledgements.ts, acknowledgements.test.ts

[P0] withdrawPurchase: a withdrawal ends the subscription first, then refunds (ST-9 engine; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4, 5.1 "Refunds and disputes", C4). Endpoints are MKT-B8, the control is MKT-B10.
CHANGE: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts: withdrawalQuote(userId, deps) and withdrawPurchase({ userId, purchaseId, actor }, deps). withdrawalQuote finds the user's latest paid Stripe charge the way refundQuote does today (server/src/features/credits/service.ts lines 747-854: the latest paid invoice of the customer; billing_reason subscription_cycle = renewal), reads the waiver consent near the charge time, the billing country on the row and, for a subscription, the period bounds from the Stripe subscription (stripePeriod), and returns { purchase: { source: 'stripe', id, planKey, chargedAt, amountMinor, currency }, decision } only when computeRefund answers rule withdrawal_14d or withdrawal_14d_prorata; otherwise null. withdrawPurchase re-computes the quote (purchaseId must match, else BillingError('withdrawal_not_available')), then: for a subscription stripe.subscriptions.cancel(subId, {}, { idempotencyKey: 'withdraw:<subId>' }) FIRST, so access ends through customer.subscription.deleted whatever amount is refunded; then issueRefund for decision.amountMinor with kind 'withdrawal' (the partial refund alone would change no access: this is the one partial refund that ends access); for a pass or pack a full issueRefund (entitlements reverse on charge.refunded). Send billing.withdrawal_confirmed (item 5) once (claim 'withdraw:<purchaseId>'). Return { status: 'withdrawn', refundMinor, currency, accessEnded: true, rule }. GoApply accounts and CN orders always get null / withdrawal_not_available (the rail has no refund call).
ACCEPT: A German subscriber with the waiver on day 5 of 30: the subscription is cancelled at once, 25/30 is refunded, Pro ends when the deleted event is processed, and one confirmation mail is sent; without the waiver the refund is full and the subscription is cancelled; calling twice sends the same two idempotency keys and refunds once; outside the 14 days the call is refused and nothing is cancelled; the cancel call always happens before the refund call.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.test.ts (order of the two Stripe calls, keys, amounts, refusal paths, replay) with the fake client.
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts, stripeRefunds.test.ts

model RABillingRefund (new, server/prisma/schema/ra-credits.prisma; additive; no relation fields so no existing model is edited):
/// One refund, withdrawal, dispute or manual CN refund (MARKET_STRATEGY ST-4, ST-9, AL-7). Idempotency stays on
/// RACreditLedger claims; this row is the readable record (history marker, admin list, dispute flag). Insert-only.
model RABillingRefund {
  id                  String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId              String
  brand               String   // 'roboapply' | 'goapply'
  rail                String   // 'stripe' | 'alipay' | 'wechatpay'
  kind                String   // 'refund' | 'withdrawal' | 'dispute' | 'manual_cn'
  /// Stripe: '<chargeId>:<amount_refunded>' or 'dispute:<disputeId>'; CN: 'order:<AlipayOrder.id>'
  externalRef         String
  chargeId            String?
  paymentIntentId     String?
  invoiceId           String?
  checkoutSessionId   String?
  alipayOrderId       String?
  planKey             String?
  amountMinor         Int
  currency            String
  full                Boolean  @default(false)
  entitlementReversed Boolean  @default(false)
  reason              String?
  /// Admin user id, 'self' (withdrawal) or 'stripe' (Dashboard refund, dispute)
  actor               String?
  note                String?  @db.Text
  createdAt           DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([rail, externalRef])
  @@index([userId, createdAt(sort: Desc)])
  @@index([invoiceId])
  @@index([alipayOrderId])
  @@index([kind, createdAt])
}

items:
[P0] Signed-in withdrawal: quote, then confirm (ST-9 server; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4 "Statutory withdrawal", M-21, Directive (EU) 2023/2673). The control is MKT-B10.
CHANGE: server/src/features/credits/routes.ts createCreditsRouter: GET /withdrawal and POST /withdrawal (seeker auth, billingRoute). service.ts: CreditsAreaService.withdrawalQuote(userId, brand) and withdraw(userId, brand, body), thin calls to withdrawalQuote and withdrawPurchase of server/src/platform/billing/stripeRefunds.ts (MKT-B6; import by file path or from the billing index, which exports them since M2), with actor 'self'; GoApply always answers available false (the mainland rails have no refund call; its published rule is on /pricing). POST is rate-limited to 3 an hour per user (this.d.rateLimit) and invalidates entitlements. The existing admin refundQuote (today lines 747-854) passes the subscription's period bounds to computeRefund so the admin quote shows the pro-rata amount too (read the Stripe subscription with stripePeriod when the latest charge is a subscription invoice). contract.ts: WithdrawBodySchema and the two response types. Contract (identical in MKT-B10): GET /api/v1/roboapply/credits/withdrawal -> { available: boolean, purchase: { source: 'stripe', id: string, planKey: string, chargedAt: string, amountMinor: number, currency: string } | null, quote: { rule: 'withdrawal_14d' | 'withdrawal_14d_prorata', refundMinor: number, currency: string, deadline: string, prorata: { usedDays: number, periodDays: number } | null, endsAccess: true, region: 'eu' | 'uk' | 'tw' } | null }. POST /api/v1/roboapply/credits/withdrawal { purchaseId: string, confirm: true } -> { status: 'withdrawn', refundMinor: number, currency: string, accessEnded: true }; errors 409 withdrawal_not_available, 429 rate_limited, 503 rail_not_configured, 502 payment_provider_error. The quote is available for 14 days after each purchase of a buyer whose billing country is in the EU, the EEA, the UK or Taiwan, with or without the waiver (the amount differs), and never for a renewal.
ACCEPT: (section 9) A German subscriber who ticked the waiver and withdraws on day 5 of 30 is quoted 25/30 of the price, the subscription is cancelled at once and Pro ends. Added: the same buyer without the waiver is quoted the full price; a US buyer and a GoApply buyer get available false; day 15 gets available false; POST with a stale purchaseId answers 409 and cancels nothing; a second POST answers 409 (already withdrawn) and refunds nothing more; the admin refund quote for the day-5 buyer shows the pro-rata amount.
TESTS: server/src/features/credits/withdrawal.test.ts (new; route harness, createFakePrisma, fake Stripe through setStripeClientForTests): the cases above, including the order "cancel, then refund" seen on the fake client; credits.test.ts (refundQuote with period bounds).
FILES: server/src/features/credits/routes.ts, service.ts, contract.ts, withdrawal.test.ts, credits.test.ts

[P0] Withdrawal without signing in: the public cancel link can preview and withdraw (ST-9 server; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4 "Cancel", "Statutory withdrawal"). The page is MKT-B10.
CHANGE: server/src/features/credits/routes.ts createPublicCancelRouter (today lines 108-127) and service.ts confirmPublicCancel (lines 564-593). Add POST /preview { token }: validates the emailed single-use token exactly as confirm does (kind billing_cancel, brand, not consumed, not expired) WITHOUT consuming it, and answers what the link can do. Extend POST /confirm with an optional withdraw: true: the token is claimed first as today; with withdraw the service runs withdrawPurchase for the quoted purchase (actor 'public_link') instead of the period-end cancel; if the withdrawal is not available any more it falls back to the ordinary cancel and says so in the answer; a provider failure releases the token as today (lines 583-591). Rate limits of the public flow are unchanged. Contract (identical in MKT-B10): POST /api/v1/public/cancel/preview { token } -> { planKey: string, accessUntil: string | null, withdrawal: { refundMinor: number, currency: string, rule: 'withdrawal_14d' | 'withdrawal_14d_prorata', deadline: string } | null }; errors 410 cancel_token_invalid. POST /api/v1/public/cancel/confirm { token, withdraw?: boolean } -> CancelResponse & { withdrawal?: { status: 'withdrawn' | 'not_available', refundMinor: number | null, currency: string | null } }. Two steps for the user (open the link, press the button) and an automatic confirmation mail (billing.withdrawal_confirmed, sent by the engine).
ACCEPT: Preview does not consume the link (confirm still works afterwards) and answers 410 for a used, expired or other-brand link; confirm with withdraw refunds and ends the subscription at once and sends the withdrawal mail; confirm without withdraw behaves exactly as today; a withdrawal that is no longer available cancels at period end and reports not_available; a Stripe failure leaves the link usable.
TESTS: server/src/features/credits/withdrawal.test.ts (public flow cases), credits.test.ts (existing public cancel cases unchanged).
FILES: server/src/features/credits/routes.ts, service.ts, contract.ts, withdrawal.test.ts

[P1] The renewal acknowledgement outlives the account: kept until the later of 3 years after consent and 1 year after the subscription ends (ST-9 "consent retention"; MARKET_STRATEGY 4.4 "Renewal", California AB 2863)
CHANGE: Today the records (SeekerConsentRecord of type auto_renew_ack, withdrawal_waiver, cn_pay_terms_ack) are deleted with the account: SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts line 221 deletes the User and the cascade removes them 30 days after a deletion request, which can be less than the law's period. New server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.ts: billingConsentRetainUntil(consentedAt, subscriptionEndedAt) = the later of consentedAt + 3 years and (subscriptionEndedAt ?? now) + 1 year; archiveBillingConsents(db, userId, now): for each billing consent record of the user's seeker profile insert one RABillingConsentArchive row (schema below) with userId, emailHash = sha256 of the lower-cased email, brand, consentType, proseHash, proseVersion, consentedAt = the record's createdAt, subscriptionEndedAt = the subscription's canceledAt or currentPeriodEnd when it is in the past, stripeCustomerId and retainUntil; rows whose retainUntil is already in the past are not written; IP address and user agent are NOT copied (the hash of the sentence is the proof). server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts: call archiveBillingConsents inside the purge, before the delete of line 221, in a way that a repeated purge run does not duplicate rows (skip when rows for that userId exist). server/src/features/compliance/retention.ts: the rule billing_consent_records (lines 437-442) now says the records are kept for that period even after the account is deleted, and a new rule billing_consent_archive deletes archive rows whose retainUntil has passed (enforcedBy 'compliance-daily', batched, brand-scoped like its neighbours; add the delegate to RetentionDb) with its English and Chinese labels next to the others (lines 490-525). BILLING_CONSENT_KEEP (line 224) stays 36 months as the minimum.
ACCEPT: A subscriber who consented 30 months ago and deletes the account today keeps an archive row until month 42 (one year after the end); one who consented 4 years ago and whose subscription ended 2 years ago leaves no row; the archive row holds no IP, no user agent and no email in clear; the daily retention run deletes a row the day after its retainUntil and not before; running the purge twice writes the rows once; the published retention schedule lists the new rule in English and Chinese.
TESTS: server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.test.ts (new: the date rule and the mapping); server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.consent.test.ts (new: archive written before deletion, idempotent; the Prisma client is mocked as in the existing purge tests); server/src/features/compliance/retention.test.ts (the new rule's sweep; the schedule text; the existing "kept minimum" assertions at lines 476-477 still hold).
FILES: server/src/platform/billing/consentArchive.ts, consentArchive.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/services/SeekerAccountPurgeService.ts, SeekerAccountPurgeService.consent.test.ts, server/src/features/compliance/retention.ts, retention.test.ts
schema:
model RABillingConsentArchive (new, server/prisma/schema/ra-credits.prisma; additive; no relation fields):
/// Checkout acknowledgements kept after the account is deleted (California AB 2863: the later of 3 years after
/// consent and 1 year after the subscription ends). Written by the account purge, removed by compliance-daily. ST-9.
model RABillingConsentArchive {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  /// The deleted account's user id (no FK) and sha256 of its lower-cased email.
  userId              String
  emailHash           String
  brand               String
  consentType         String    // 'auto_renew_ack' | 'withdrawal_waiver' | 'cn_pay_terms_ack'
  proseHash           String?
  proseVersion        String?
  consentedAt         DateTime
  subscriptionEndedAt DateTime?
  stripeCustomerId    String?
  retainUntil         DateTime
  createdAt           DateTime  @default(now())

  @@index([retainUntil])
  @@index([emailHash])
  @@index([userId])
}

(1) AL-3 and AL-4 (rollout phase A) are in M2: they need rails/rails.test.ts, whose StripeRail block MKT-B1 must rewrite in M1 (ST-0, PC-1, ST-2), and nothing depends on them before the AL-8 cut-over.
